data.narrative:
Collaborative Robotics, founded by Brad Porter, is a Series B robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $150M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws from a peer set of 4 primary comparables in the same sector and stage—Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B Series B), Hadrian ($1.6B Series C), and Nimble Robotics ($1.0B Series C)—supplemented by a broader universe of 8 private peers and 1 public comparable.

Two triangulation methods apply. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier to the company's last post-money valuation of $500M, implying $950M. Peer-median analysis across the 4 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields a median valuation of $1.6B, with a range of $1.0B to $1.8B. These methods produce meaningfully different signals, reflecting variance in peer stage and market conditions.

The triangulated analysis across both methods supports a valuation range of $808M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $1.3B. Key uncertainties include the company's revenue trajectory and capital efficiency relative to Bedrock and Dexterity, both at higher valuations in the same stage, and the applicability of Series C comps to a Series B round. The $1.1B spread between low and high reflects legitimate differences in comparable selection and stage adjustment methodology.
